newsitem.title: GERMANY: GOLF-CAMPBELL THANKS MR MAGIC FOR HIS RETURN TO FORM.
newsitem.headline: GOLF-CAMPBELL THANKS MR MAGIC FOR HIS RETURN TO FORM.

text.p: Struggling Michael Campbell paid tribute on Friday to a Belgian sports psychologist dubbed 'Mr Magic' for ending the worst period of his short career.

The New Zealander shot a five-under 67 in the second round of the European Tournament Players Championship on Friday to signal the end of a barren spell in which he had missed seven of his last eight cuts.
The 28-year-old came on to the European Tour in a blaze of glory in his first full season in 1995 after qualifying from the European Challenge Tour.

Two years ago he finished fifth on the European rankings without winning an event but stirring the golfing world by leading the British Open going into the final round. Last year, though, he lost his touch through injury and lost his tour card, finishing 120th on the rankings and having to rely mainly on invitations this year.

After a bright start, though, Campbell's form steadily deteriorated. But through counselling with his sports psychologist Joss Vantisphout, nicknamed Mr Magic by European Tour professionals because of his ability to talk them into playing better, Campbell ended his awful run with a six-birdie round at Gut Kaden.

"It's great to make a cut again and I hope this now snowballs," said Campbell. "I've been pondering too much in the past. But working with Joss he's encouraged me to work on not just the present but the future, helped me block out the negative thoughts and concentrate where I am at the moment.

"I think I mentally kept making excuses for my bad form. I've had my coach with me, too, but really it wasn't the swing at fault but mental pressure. When you keep thinking about how well you'd played in the past you tend then to try too hard."
